verdict: Aon's revenue grew 3% to $4.1B — 6% once divestitures are stripped out — as risk advice boomed, while heavy spending on its growth program held reported operating profit flat at $809M.

segments.name: Commercial Risk Solutions
segments.note: Insurance brokerage and risk advice for companies — Aon's biggest business, up 6% on new business and strong retention.

segments.name: Health Solutions
segments.note: Employee health-benefits advice and administration, up 6%.

segments.name: Reinsurance Solutions
segments.note: Helping insurers themselves buy insurance (reinsurance) and manage risk — up 7%.

segments.name: Wealth Solutions
segments.note: Retirement and investment advice. Down 21%, mostly because Aon sold the NFP Wealth business (shown here net of $2M of eliminations).

opex.name: Other general expense
opex.note: Outside services, professional fees and other running costs.

opex.name: Technology, premises & depreciation
opex.note: IT ($156M), offices ($83M) and depreciation of equipment ($49M).

opex.name: Amortization & impairment
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time (a non-cash charge).

opex.name: Accelerating Aon United program
opex.note: The cost of Aon's multi-year restructuring and growth program — up from $32M a year ago.

otherDetail: Interest expense on Aon's debt and other non-operating items cost $197M, net.
footerNote: Aon reports no cost-of-revenue line; following professional-services practice, the chart treats compensation and benefits ($2,275M — the people who deliver the service) as the direct cost. Net income of $486M includes $10M attributable to noncontrolling interests; $476M was attributable to Aon shareholders.

takeaways.title: Underlying growth is stronger than the headline
takeaways.text: Reported revenue rose 3% to $4.1B, but that is after losing revenue from sold businesses. Organic growth — the same business, like for like — was 6%, led by Commercial Risk (+7% organic) on new business wins and high retention.

takeaways.title: A growth program is eating reported profit
takeaways.text: Operating income was flat at $809M even though revenue grew, because spending on the Accelerating Aon United program nearly tripled to $93M. Excluding that program and acquisition amortization, adjusted operating income rose 5% to $1,106M.

takeaways.title: Wealth shrank after a business sale
takeaways.text: Wealth Solutions revenue fell 21% to $429M, almost entirely because Aon sold NFP's wealth business. The flip side: the sales recycle cash into Aon's faster-growing risk and health franchises.

oneTimers: Operating expenses include $93M for the Accelerating Aon United restructuring program (vs $32M a year ago) and $175M of amortization and impairment of acquisition intangibles. Aon's adjusted EPS of $3.36 excludes these items.
